extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians considering submitting research or survey articles to the Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society (authors, prospective authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for preparing and submitting concise research articles, survey articles, and obituaries to the Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society, including scope, length limits, peer-review model, and open-access options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and purpose of articles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society focuses on the publication of concise articles reporting a significant advance in mathematical knowledge, or which are deemed to stimulate new interest and research activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should target concise presentations that either report a significant advance or are likely to stimulate new interest and research activity. The Bulletin shares an editorial board with the Journal of the London Mathematical Society but prioritises shorter, concise contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum length for research articles
rubrics_metrics.description: The articles have a maximum length of 20 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure research articles do not exceed 20 pages. Note the Journal of the London Mathematical Society publishes longer research articles (18 pages and above), so authors with longer manuscripts should consider the sister journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable content types
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to primary research articles, the Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society also publishes authoritative survey articles (of any length) and obituaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare submissions according to the appropriate category (research article, survey article, or obituary). Survey articles and obituaries have different expectations (see separate entry for survey articles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey article standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Each survey article should be an in-depth, authoritative overview of the state of the subject, of interest to newcomers as well as experts and, ideally, one that would become a standard reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey articles may contain full proofs, pieces of original research or unorthodox points of view on known results, and can be of any length. Since January 2020 most survey articles have been published open access subject to the authors' agreement. The Managing Editors welcome submissions of survey articles via the Bulletin EditFlow site, selecting 'Survey Article' as the special category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review policy and potential for editorial rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles published in this journal are peer reviewed. Editors may reject papers without external review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware of desk-rejection risk and consult the full peer review policy for details. The Bulletin states it employs a high standard of peer review shared with the Journal of the London Mathematical Society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity and interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity transparency: Single anonymised. Reviewer interacts with: Editor. Review information published: None.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewing model is single-anonymised (reviewers know authors? — standard interpretation: reviewers are anonymous to authors). Reviewers communicate with the handling editor rather than directly with authors, and review reports are not published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access and funder-compliance options
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society is a hybrid open access journal. By default, articles in the journal will be published on a subscription basis and only be accessible to journal subscribers. The journal has options for gold and green open access publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submitting, authors should check any open access requirements from their institution or funder. If required to publish open access but a compliant route cannot be identified with the Bulletin, authors should contact the journal team before submitting. See the journal's open access page for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission practicalities and recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting an article to the Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society, we recommend that authors read the submission guidelines for the Bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Bulletin EditFlow submission site for submitting (especially for survey articles choose the 'Survey Article' special category). Contact lmsjournals@lms.ac.uk for queries about submitting, articles under review, the peer review process or the submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance production process
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is accepted for publication in the Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society, it will be sent to the publisher for typesetting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For accepted articles which have not been passed to the publisher for production, contact the LMS team at production@lms.ac.uk. For accepted articles which have been passed to Wiley for production, contact the Wiley team at blms@wiley.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership access and activation
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the London Mathematical Society can receive free online access to the Bulletin (and two other journals) if they have signed up for free online access via their LMS membership record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activate free online access by visiting www.lms.ac.uk/user and selecting the preferred journals under the 'My LMS Membership' tab; the LMS will notify Wiley to issue credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal positioning relative to sister journals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulletin shares an Editorial Board with the Journal of the London Mathematical Society. The Journal publishes longer research articles (18 pages and above) while the Bulletin focuses on concise articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should choose the most appropriate outlet (Bulletin vs Journal vs Proceedings vs Transactions) depending on length, scope, and the desired audience/impact; Proceedings is the flagship for highest-impact articles of broad interest, Transactions is fully open access across full range of mathematics.
